purpose: Show a founder that a developer from our team can work inside theirs full time, what that costs next to hiring locally (sourced, like for like), what the monthly price covers, how a week runs and how the hours line up, then get them to describe the role.

A band of four or five parallel satin ribbons in Partner Navy and slate blue flows from the lower left to the upper right, the partner's own team. A single brighter satin ribbon in a gradient from Alliance Blue to Ribbon Cyan enters from the left edge, weaves over and under the navy ribbons and settles into the band as one of them, so the band continues to the right as one team with the bright ribbon inside it. Low flat faceted paper hills in pale Daylight blues sit beneath. Keep the weave in the centre of the frame so it crops cleanly to 4:5, and keep the top quarter calm and open. Square 1:1, safe to crop to 4:5. Palette only: Partner Navy #121B2A, Alliance Blue #1B56FF, Ribbon Cyan #00D5FF, Daylight #F4F7FB and the shades between them. sections.name: Time zones
sections.job: Show how a morning in Manila lines up with Sydney, New York and London and what that means for each market, with sources.
sections.desktop: Navy chapter. Heading/1 head, the Time zones component (sample November moment), a sample-time note, three hairline rows (country + source key | what it means), two mono sources. Row text starts on the lead's column and stays 620 px wide (about 75 characters).
sections.mobile: Head, the 2x2 Time zones variant, note, rows stacked (country above text), sources.

content.heading: On your hours, wherever you are.
content.lead: Our day overlaps yours in Australia and the UK. For US partners, the work moves while you sleep: brief us before you log off, and see progress when you log on.

items.title: Australia [1]
items.text: Sydney is two hours ahead of us, or three during Australian daylight saving, so our working days overlap.

items.title: United States [2]
items.text: You are 12 to 16 hours behind us. Keep your hours, or brief your developer before you log off and see progress when you log on.

items.title: United Kingdom [2]
items.text: You are seven or eight hours behind us. Our afternoon is your morning.

body: Sample times for a November morning in Manila (Manila 9:41 am, Sydney 12:41 pm, New York 8:41 pm the day before, London 1:41 am). The live site shows the real time in each city.

sources.text: NSW Government, Daylight saving (Sydney is UTC+10, or UTC+11 in daylight saving). Retrieved 2026-11-02.
NIST, Local time FAQs (US time zones and daylight saving). Retrieved 2026-11-02.

content.heading: Questions buyers ask
content.lead: Straight answers about working with an embedded developer. If yours isn’t here, ask us directly.

faq.q: Who manages the developer day to day?
faq.a: You do. They join your stand-ups, take work from your board and follow your team’s process. We handle their employment, benefits and equipment.

faq.q: What does the monthly price include?
faq.a: Their pay and benefits, recruiting and equipment. You get a fixed quote before they start.

faq.q: What if it isn’t working out?
faq.a: Tell us early, and we will work it out with you.
You do. The work happens in your repositories and accounts, and you own what they build.
AI takes over the repetitive hours, and a person still reviews every piece of work before it reaches you. We cost less because our team is based in the Philippines.
Yes. Monthly plans can be canceled with [30] days’ notice.
